ops.title: Campaign cap enforcement: three confirmed gaps vs v0.7.1 (codex runtime repros)
ops.description:
Final cross-repo review 2026-07-18; all three CONFIRMED by codex runtime reproductions against released 0.7.1. Filed as records — the tree is operator-active (sample()/sampler_path WIP), so no agent fix dispatched.

1. Crash-resume recompute undercounts overshooting spend (meta.py:221 / loop.py:684 / meta.py:611). A run that durably journals $4 actual against a $3 reservation, then crashes after journal+settle but before the ABORTED ledger row, resumes counting only $3: repro printed {ledger_total: 3.0, durable_actual: 4.0, refusal: None, actual_plus_new_reservation: 6.0} against a $5 cap — a new $2 reservation was admitted.

2. A surviving accounting-abort latch does not gate the OUTER campaign loop (meta.py:737 / procs.py:388 / loop.py:619). After settle fails twice and the <experiment>.abort.json latch lands, restart's procs scan marks the record accounted; run_campaign sees no orphan and advances to the NEXT sequence while the latch persists: repro {latch_survives: True, seq2_completed: True}. Breaks the security-model claim 'a durable abort latch refuses startup until reconciled' at the assembled-loop level.

3. max_wall_s reservation excludes preflight time that settlement then bills (loop.py:632 / meta.py:586 / meta.py:656): 0.5s reservation + 1s preflight settled 1.387s, breaching both the per-run reservation and the campaign wall cap on a successful run.

ops.text: crash-resume recompute reconciles durable journal actuals against ledger reservations (repro: 4.0 actual vs 3.0 reserved no longer admits a breach)
campaign start/resume refuses new launches while any unreconciled *.abort.json latch survives
preflight time is inside the wall reservation contract (0.5s cap + 1s preflight can no longer settle 1.39s on a completed run)
